summary: Customer saw far fewer scanned pages than indexed (e.g. 185 vs 1,100 on Ulster Bank /business, 590 vs 1,900 on RBS) and erratic month-to-month page counts on NatWest properties.
mechanism: Two factors per support: (1) seed list/crawl config drifted between runs (different seed sets, axe settings toggled), so runs are not comparable; (2) customer site rate-limits the crawler - many HTTP 429s in crawl logs, throttled pages dropped. Also many URLs were PDFs/XLS (non-HTML) counted as failures. Deep root cause confirmed later in follow-up #2914 (429s at subresource level + timeouts lose link extraction).
resolution: Explained; advised stable seed list / sitemap-based seeds, locking crawl config, and allowlisting crawler (EvincedBot UA or 5 static NAT IPs). Customer escalated to Adobe (host); continued in #2914.

summary: Authenticated property indexed only 1 page (login/mailbox page); crawler did not get past it to other sections.
mechanism: Login actually succeeded; the AngularJS webmail app's nav links are href="javascript:void(0);" with ng-click handlers (hash routes), so there are no URLs for the crawler to follow. (--disable-web-security toggle was tried with no effect.)
resolution: Switched property to list mode/seed list with the customer-supplied hash-route URLs (#/mail/..., #/calendar, #/preferences/...); crawl and scan succeeded.

summary: Customer's properties for verizon.com/business sections pulled wrong URLs (e.g. 3,919 of 4,293 pages outside /business; Mobile property pulled all /business pages instead of /business/products/mobile); asked Evinced to build TK_EV_ copies that work.

resolution: Evinced created TK_EV_ copy properties and refined the regexes/scope until output matched (Mobile -> only /business/products/mobile, 17 pages); walkthrough call held. Jira CS-2728 done.

summary: Customer reported Site Scanner scanning pre-redirect (client-side JS redirect) URLs producing false positives (html-has-lang, viewport), plus page counts jumping (5,000 -> 943 on Stores, 4 -> ~5,000 on My Access).
mechanism: Established: old URLs are soft-404s (URL stays, content shows 'can't find that page', no redirect) so they load as valid pages and get scanned; My Access property scope had been widened to all of www.verizon.com and seeded with dead /my-access-rewards URLs (change from a customer IP, no audit log), causing ~5,000 pages; relative href="banner" link in the Transcend cookie-consent dialog resolves against every page producing /banner 404 pages. Stores 5,000->943 drop not explained. Scanner does follow real redirects.
resolution: Explained; recommended removing stale seed URLs and an exclude regex like .*/banner/?$ (or dismissing consent dialog before link extraction as done in #2172). Feature requests: audit log of property changes (CS-1751), non-URL-based exclusion / soft-404 detection (CS-2360 context). Ticket kept on hold.

summary: Follow-up to #2185: natwest.com page coverage swung wildly month to month (3,264 / 1,152 / 4,518 / 731 / 3,164 / 1,828) vs ~3,500+ sitemap pages; rbs.co.uk stuck at fixed count.
mechanism: Site rate-limits the crawler: 22-58% of requests got HTTP 429 plus ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM; pages that fail/time out (up to 91s loads, 1,384 timeouts in a ~5h July run with reuseBrowser off) yield no outbound links so discovery stalls and varies per run. Crawler does not read sitemap.xml. Property was not on the static NAT pool (traffic came from ephemeral GCP IP). rbs.co.uk had 'Crawl before scan' disabled so it rescanned a June-2024 crawl list. Later: two properties scheduled at the same time on same site triggered 429s causing error-page false positives.
resolution: Moved property to speed-tier.slow (one request at a time) -> 4,615 pages, 0 errors; enabled static NAT IPs; recrawled rbs.co.uk and set slow tier (2,593 pages); excluded 403 editor URLs; suggested staggering schedules. Separate engine FP (anchor without href on breadcrumb) fixed in CS-2847 / analysis-web 16.34.12.
